overall: Atlanta is starting the morning fully overcast (OVC, 100% cloud fraction, ceiling only 213m/~700 ft) with a current temperature of 77°F and a very high dewpoint of 71.6°F, indicating a humid and sluggish warming pattern so far. Despite a 30-minute velocity of +3.6°F/hr suggesting some recent acceleration, the persistent low cloud deck is suppressing morning heating and represents the biggest departure from what models anticipated. Afternoon thunderstorms (40% chance after 1pm) add a timing wildcard that could cap the daily high if convection fires early.
forecast_obs_notes: There is meaningful model spread: HRRR and the NWS text forecast both target near 89°F, while NBM comes in at 86.6°F and ECMWF at a more conservative 85.2°F — the ECMWF may be weighting the current cloud/moisture burden more heavily. max_temp_prediction: The most likely outcome is a daily high in the 88-90°F range, with the central estimate near 88.5°F. The primary drivers are: NWS and HRRR alignment around 89°F, META model probability mass peaking at 88-91°F, and southwesterly flow supporting afternoon warmth. The key downside risk is the current overcast deck with a very low ceiling — if clouds are slow to clear, peak heating will be truncated and a high closer to 86-87°F (ECMWF territory) becomes plausible. Upside beyond 90°F is possible but constrained by moisture, cloud cover, and the afternoon storm threat. Confidence is moderate.
